newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big spreads in Morris, Homestake.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big spreads in Morris, Homestake.

text.p: A two-way call spread in Philip Morris Cos Inc and a four-way put spread in long-term options on shares of Homestake Mining Co highlighted equity options trading Wednesday as the broad market extended its sharp rally, traders said.
The Philip Morris September 45 call traded about 11,825 contracts and the September 50 call traded 12,350. Open interest in the 45 was 9,930 and in the 50 was 8,736.
In afternoon trading, Philip Morris shares were unchanged at 39-1/4 on turnover of roughly 5.4 million shares.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said an investor bought the September 45 calls and sold the September 50s.
"I don't know what that's going to do, but he's very bullish," Roth said.
The September 45 calls were trading up 3/16 at two and the 50s were down 3/16 at one.
The spread in Homestake Mining options involved the January 1998 15 and 17-1/2 puts and the January 1999 12-1/2 and 15 puts.
The January 1998 15 traded about 8,400 contracts, the January 1998 17-1/2 traded 4,650, the January 1999 12-1/2 traded 9,300 and the January 1999 15 traded about 4,660.

"It was a customer who comes in periodically and does usually three-, four- or five-way spreads involving LEAPS (long-term equity anticipation securities)," one trader said. "For him I think it was basically a roll."
He said the investor was likely closing some positions and opening others and that the investor commonly is short on a ratio basis the out-of-the-money puts.
Homestake shares were unchanged at 13-1/4 in afternoon trading.
In other activity, options on Cisco Systems were busy as investors began to take positions ahead of the company's earnings, which are due out next Tuesday, traders said.
"Network stocks have been hammered down pretty good," said Patrick Hamilton at LETCO in Chicago. "From what it looks like to me, they're anticipating maybe some good numbers."
The Cisco May 50 call traded about 6,855 contracts, the May 55 call traded 6,335 and the May 60 call traded 2,745.
Among the Cisco May puts, the 45-strike puts were most active with volume of nearly 6,300 contracts.
Cisco was up 2-1/2 at 52-1/2 as the technology sector continued its recovery from its recent selloff.
Hamilton said volatility in the Cisco options was declining as the stock moved higher, but that it could pick up early next week heading into the earnings.

"Monday and Tuesday, chances are that the volatility will come up," he said. "However, how much it comes up depends on which way the stock goes. If it starts heading south, then the volatility's going to come right back up."
